PullRequest.Title: sessions: Add experimental chat-scoped layout modes
PullRequest.Body:

Adds experimental chat-scoped layout to the Agents Window while retaining the existing session-scoped layout implementation.

### Behavior

`sessions.experimental.layoutScope` is window-scoped and takes effect after manually reloading the window:

| Mode | Editors and selected panel view | Editor/Details composition and bottom-panel visibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session-shared` (default) | Per session | Shared Existing visibility profiles (unchanged behavior) |
| `chat-shared` | Per chat | Shared Existing preference across workspace-backed sessions/chats |
| `chat` | Per chat | Per chat |

The existing desktop controller, draft/existing lifecycle strategies and editor working-set machinery are reused with scope-aware state keys. Geometry and the sidebar remain window-owned. Terminal and task behavior is unchanged in all modes; no terminal ownership metadata is introduced.

### Implementation

- Capture and restore ordinary editors, active editor and selected panel view when switching sibling chats.
- Persist composition and last-open state separately from shared geometry, with separate stores for each mode.
- Handle confirmed chat deletion, session archive/removal and draft promotion without dropping delayed-catalog state or releasing still-referenced working-set handles.
- Suspend chat-owned projection during phone presentation and resume the focused owner on desktop.
- Guard queued Details-only collapse against stale owners and changed visibility.
- Retain collapsed ordinary editors by chat, transfer main-chat composition on draft promotion, and reconstruct persisted peer ownership without requiring the peer to be visited after reload.
- Add isolated scenario-launch environment, Agents profile settings and native-window resizing support for recorded validation.

### Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed after review fixes, before the naming-only rename from `session` to `session-shared`.
- `npm run hygiene` — passed after review fixes, before the naming-only rename; commit hygiene passed for the rename.
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed after the mode rename.
- `node node_modules/@typescript/native/bin/tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --pretty false` — passed after the mode rename.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser/*.test.js'` — 261 passed after the mode rename.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/common/chatLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/terminal/test/browser/sessionsTerminalContribution.test.ts` — 95 passed after the mode rename.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/test/browser/changesViewService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/common/chatLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/terminal/test/browser/sessionsTerminalContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts` — 503 passed, 2 pending after review fixes.
- `npm --prefix test/scenario run compile` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed before review fixes; fixes add no cross-layer dependencies.

Review regressions were exercised before their fixes: 16 failed and 3 baseline/same-resource cases passed. All 19 added cases pass after the fixes. The workspace-hydration test explicitly verifies Editor and Details visibility, preserving upstream empty-group/default-tab rules.

Earlier isolated local Code OSS recordings passed 13 terminal/layout checks per mode (39 total), including shared session terminals, targeted disposal and local shell PID preservation through renderer reload. Those recordings predate the latest upstream merge, review fixes and naming-only rename from `session` to `session-shared`. Mobile-platform coverage and full-process restart remain unverified; renderer reload is not a substitute for process restart.

### Manual testing

1. Use the Agents Window with a workspace-backed session and two sibling chats.
2. Select each layout scope in Settings and manually reload.
3. Open and pin different files in each chat; switch between them and verify editor/active-tab restoration.
4. Change Editor/Details composition, bottom-panel visibility and selected panel view. Verify the scope described above, including hide/reopen.
5. Reload, then exercise chat deletion, session archive and draft submission. Confirm surviving owners retain their state.
6. Confirm existing terminal behavior remains the same in all modes.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed key now follows activeChat, so each sibling-chat transition reaches _applyWorkingSet. That method queues through Sequencer, which runs every task in order, and its stale-owner checks occur only after applyWorkingSet has completed. EditorParts.applyWorkingSet disposes groups, restores grid state, and reopens editors. The added test explicitly asserts that both superseded and superseding applies run to completion, eliminating uncertainty about the mechanism; only real-world editor counts and switch burst length affect magnitude.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, editor-group/DOM reconstruction, and editor reopen operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A burst of N chat selections queues N complete working-set applications; each application scales with the groups and editors in that owner's snapshot, and the final selected chat waits behind all N-1 obsolete restores.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked final chat-switch completion, excess CPU/GC work, and visible editor churn or dropped frames during rapid navigation
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, the working-set derive was keyed only by session resource, so switching sibling chats in the same session did not enqueue editor working-set applications.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The derive now emits a chat owner key and the added line invokes _applyWorkingSet for every owner transition; _workingSetSequencer serializes all requests without replacing stale queued owners.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 512 changes restoration from session resource to the newly chat-scoped `current.key`, placing every sibling-chat focus change onto the full applyWorkingSet path.
Findings.Title: Coalesce superseded chat working-set restores
Findings.Impact: Clicking or keyboard-navigating quickly across sibling chats with saved editors makes the final chat wait while intermediate, no-longer-visible chats fully tear down and reconstruct the editor area.
Findings.Evidence: The changed line schedules every current.key through _applyWorkingSet. _applyWorkingSet uses Sequencer, whose queue chains every task rather than coalescing. Its isStaleChatOwner checks are after IEditorGroupsService.applyWorkingSet. EditorParts.applyWorkingSet disposes groups, applies serialized grid state, and reopens editors. The added R4 test asserts `['empty', 'empty']` with the message that both superseded and superseding applies must run to completion.
Findings.Recommendation: Use latest-owner scheduling for pending restores (or check the captured owner snapshot before starting a queued apply) so only the active apply plus the newest requested owner can run; preserve the existing post-await stale guard for an already in-flight restore.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added owner-change listener is specific to same-session chat transitions and directly invokes _saveWorkingSet. That helper synchronously deletes the prior handle and saves a replacement; EditorParts.deleteWorkingSet and saveWorkingSet each call saveWorkingSets(), which JSON.stringify's the entire editorWorkingSets collection, while saveWorkingSet also serializes the current editor grid. Storage's database flush is deferred, but the snapshot construction and two full serializations happen synchronously. The only magnitude uncertainty is the typical number and size of retained chat working sets.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Editor-grid snapshot objects and JSON bytes for the complete editorWorkingSets collection
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each sibling-chat focus transition performs O(E) current-grid snapshot work plus two O(W) serializations of all saved working-set state, where E is the outgoing editor tree and W is the accumulated state across retained chat owners; repeated A/B switching repeats this unchanged work every time.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased renderer CPU/GC pressure and synchronous chat-switch latency as the number of chats and saved editors grows
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, same-session activeChat changes did not change activeSession and therefore did not call _saveWorkingSet; working sets were rebuilt only when switching sessions or saving at shutdown.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new ChatLayoutContext runOnChange handler calls _saveWorkingSet for the previous owner on every sibling-chat owner change, even when that owner's editor set and active tab have not changed since its previous capture.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 302 is inside the newly added ChatLayoutContext owner-change listener and adds `this._saveWorkingSet(key)` for sibling-chat changes; this path did not exist when ownership was session-scoped.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding every working-set snapshot on each chat switch
Findings.Impact: Rapidly switching among sibling chats with several retained editor sets repeatedly serializes the whole working-set catalog twice per switch on the UI thread, making chat navigation increasingly sluggish and allocation-heavy.
Findings.Evidence: At the changed line, every same-session previous.owner/current.owner transition calls _saveWorkingSet(key). _saveWorkingSet first calls _deleteWorkingSet and then IEditorGroupsService.saveWorkingSet. EditorParts.deleteWorkingSet splices and calls saveWorkingSets(); saveWorkingSet builds mainPart.createState()/auxiliary state, appends it, and also calls saveWorkingSets(); saveWorkingSets synchronously JSON.stringify's the full editorWorkingSets array. IStorageService only defers the eventual backing-store flush, not these serializations.
Findings.Recommendation: Track whether the focused owner's editor resources/active editor changed and reuse its existing handle when clean; when dirty, replace/update it once rather than delete-and-save two full catalog snapshots on every focus transition.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new peer-cleanup method loops every owner key and calls _deleteWorkingSet. Each unique handle reaches EditorParts.deleteWorkingSet, which immediately calls saveWorkingSets and synchronously JSON.stringify's the entire remaining global working-set array. Session removal/archive supplies all peer keys at once, so the repeated shrinking-catalog rewrites and quadratic scaling are directly established; uncertainty is limited to how many sibling chats users retain in one session.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU and temporary JSON strings for the global editor working-set catalog
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Removing or archiving a session with K peer chat owners performs up to K deleteWorkingSet calls; each serializes the remaining O(K) working-set collection, producing O(K²) aggregate serialization/allocation for that lifecycle event, plus any unrelated owners in the global catalog.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased archive/removal latency and renderer CPU/GC pressure for sessions with many retained sibling-chat editor sets
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before chat-scoped ownership, a session had one working-set handle, so archive/removal performed at most one delete and one catalog serialization for that session.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new _forgetPeerChatState loop deletes every peer owner's working-set handle individually, and onDidChangeSessions invokes it with the complete peer-key set for an archived or removed session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 769 is in the newly added peer-owner cleanup loop and invokes `_deleteWorkingSet(key)` once per chat key; the pre-diff session cleanup deleted only `session.resource` once.
Findings.Title: Batch working-set cleanup when removing a chat-heavy session
Findings.Impact: Archiving or removing a session after using many sibling chats can synchronously rewrite the full editor-working-set payload once per chat, causing a noticeable UI pause and allocation spike.
Findings.Evidence: The added loop calls _deleteWorkingSet once for each key. _deleteWorkingSet releases each unique handle through IEditorGroupsService.deleteWorkingSet. EditorParts.deleteWorkingSet splices one item and immediately calls saveWorkingSets(), whose implementation JSON.stringify's the entire editorWorkingSets array into workspace storage. onDidChangeSessions calls _forgetPeerChatState(_chatLayoutOwnerKeys.forgetSession(...)), so one session lifecycle event fans out across all retained peers.
Findings.Recommendation: Collect all unreferenced handles for the session and remove them through a batched editor-working-set operation that persists the catalog once; if batching requires an explicit editor-groups dependency, defer or coalesce these lifecycle deletions rather than issuing one persisted delete per owner.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switching between sibling chats in an experimental desktop layout mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: activeChat changes -> ChatLayoutContext owner change -> synchronous outgoing working-set delete/save -> chat-keyed restore scheduling -> IEditorGroupsService.applyWorkingSet -> final editor state. Snapshot construction and JSON serialization are on the critical path; the backing storage flush is deferred.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the outgoing editor grid, then stringify the entire editorWorkingSets catalog once for delete and once for save
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two full-catalog JSON serializations per sibling-chat transition, plus current-grid serialization; repeated for every switch
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sibling activeChat changes did not save a session-scoped working set because activeSession did not change
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation before the switch can progress

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose editor groups, apply serialized grid state, and reopen editors for the selected working set
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete apply per chat selection, including every superseded queued selection
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same-session sibling-chat focus changes did not invoke applyWorkingSet
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The final selected chat waits for all earlier queued reconstructions

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update workspace-storage cache/pending inserts for editor.workingSets and schedule a deferred flush
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two storage cache updates per outgoing save; underlying flushes are scheduled and may coalesce
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No editor-working-set storage updates on sibling-chat focus changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The backing-store flush is off the critical path, but value comparison/cache update occurs after synchronous JSON construction

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rapid chat selections, retained chat working sets, and editors/groups serialized in each working set. Effective cardinality is one outgoing save and one incoming apply per owner transition, including intermediate transitions that are already stale.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Outgoing saves run synchronously. Incoming restores use one global Sequencer, so they are serialized but not coalesced; a burst queues every intermediate owner and the final owner waits behind them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The owner map caches handles and warm incoming owners reuse a handle for apply, but outgoing owners are destructively deleted and recreated even when unchanged. Cold first visits apply an empty set; warm visits still perform full restore. No negative-cache behavior is relevant.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines, editor implementation, Sequencer semantics, and an added test that requires superseded applies to complete establish the mechanisms.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical sibling-chat counts and editor payload sizes vary, but the per-transition double serialization and uncoalesced full apply are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: one finding covers repeated synchronous working-set rebuilding and one covers missing coalescing of stale editor restores.

Scenarios.Scenario: Closing, reopening, or changing Editor/Details composition per chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Part visibility/toggle event -> capture current or pre-hide composition -> enumerate owner map -> JSON.stringify -> storage cache update. Database flush is deferred.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate and stringify the complete current/pre-hide composition map
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or several small catalog serializations per user toggle depending on strategy events
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy mode persisted a constant-size shared visibility profile rather than a per-owner catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous but payload entries are small and the event is user-driven

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the composition JSON in workspace storage and schedule its flush
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache update per _save; flush is deferred and may coalesce
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the constant-size legacy profile was stored
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Backing database work is off the critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of retained owner composition entries and number of visibility/toggle events; each entry is only a URI plus two booleans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event listeners; storage flushes are deferred/coalesced, with no parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The in-memory ResourceMap serves reads, but set/setPreHide do not equality-check and serialize the complete catalog. Confirmed deletion and session archive remove entries; hidden tabs intentionally remain cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for serialization placement, lower for material impact at realistic catalog sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large long-lived chat catalogs could increase this cost, but entries are tiny and realistic toggle frequency did not establish a separate high-confidence user-visible regression beyond the reported working-set paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: lifecycle cleanup exists and the tiny, user-driven payload did not meet the reporting threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reloading a desktop Agents window with persisted chat layout state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench storage is loaded -> controller synchronously reads and parses versioned layout/composition records -> registers persisted owner keys -> restores only the focused owner's composition/working set.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.parse and validate versioned layout and composition catalogs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parse per selected layout-state key and up to two composition keys per window construction
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy startup parsed one session-layout array and one constant-size visibility profile
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during controller startup before owner restoration

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: IStorageService.get call sites in layout stores
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded number of key reads; backing storage initialization is pre-existing
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads are from the storage service cache on this path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of retained chat owners and serialized URI/editor state bytes across the selected mode.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Startup parsing is synchronous; active working-set restoration is serialized. Non-focused owners are loaded as metadata but not applied.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold controller construction parses storage once; subsequent owner reads use ResourceMaps. Separate keys isolate chat and chat-shared modes. Malformed records are removed rather than retried.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the one-time parse path and lack of network/filesystem fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size depends on retained chats, but this is one-time linear startup work with exact-owner cleanup on deletion/archive.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: startup work is linear, bounded by retained owner state, and avoids eager application of every owner.

Scenarios.Scenario: Archiving or removing a session with many retained sibling-chat layouts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: onDidChangeSessions -> gather all peer owner keys -> loop _deleteWorkingSet -> EditorParts.deleteWorkingSet -> stringify the shrinking global working-set catalog for each peer -> finish lifecycle notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stringify the complete remaining editorWorkingSets array after each individual peer-handle deletion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to K full-catalog serializations for one session lifecycle event, yielding quadratic aggregate bytes for K peer-owned sets
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session cleanup deleted one session-scoped working-set handle
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks archive/removal event handling and causes synchronous allocation/GC pressure

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update the editor.workingSets storage cache and schedule flush after each deletion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to K cache updates; underlying flushes may coalesce
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: At most one storage update for the session's handle
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Database flush is deferred, but each full JSON value is built synchronously

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number K of peer chats with unique saved working-set handles and total editor state retained across all working sets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entire cleanup loop is synchronous and serial; no batching or backpressure consolidates persistence.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reference checks preserve shared/legacy handles, but every unique peer handle is immediately removed and persisted separately. Composition cleanup batches keys into at most one save per map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cleanup fan-out and per-delete full serialization are directly implemented.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most sessions may have few peers, but the quadratic mechanism is deterministic for chat-heavy sessions.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary-fanout finding; cleanup should persist once for all unreferenced handles.

Scenarios.Scenario: Confirmed chat deletion and draft/session replacement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing provider delete request completes -> enriched local deletion event forgets the exact owner, or replacement remaps local owner maps and working-set references. No new provider request is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider call per user deletion, unchanged by the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider delete call was awaited before firing the old event
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still gates successful deletion; event payload construction is local and negligible

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist composition maps when exact owner state is forgotten/remapped
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one rewrite per changed map for a single chat; session-wide archive behavior is covered separately
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous local work after lifecycle confirmation

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One deleted chat, or the number of peer owner keys remapped for one replaced session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The provider operation remains one awaited request. Local map cleanup/remap is synchronous; per-session remap is linear.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact successful deletion invalidates one owner; failed deletion emits nothing. Replacement transfers cached state. Persisted peers are registered even before catalog hydration, avoiding miss retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call cardinality and exact cleanup behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider duration is provider-specific but unchanged; local single-chat cleanup is small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the external boundary count is unchanged and single-chat cleanup is bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launching and resizing recorded validation scenarios
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Scenario runner seeds profile files -> starts one existing Electron/browser application with optional environment overrides -> optional resize uses one Electron bridge evaluation or browser viewport call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/write built-in Agents profile settings in addition to regular user settings
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra mkdir/write pair only when userSettings, --agents, and desktop are all present
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the regular profile settings file was written
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the test application starts

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the Electron/browser application with environment overrides
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch as before; extraEnv changes arguments, not process count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same application process was launched without per-run extraEnv

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Evaluate BrowserWindow.getSize/setSize through Playwright's Electron handle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bridge evaluation per explicit resize step
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native resize helper was exposed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only affects test automation progress, not product runtime

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One scenario launch, size of userSettings, and explicit number of resize steps.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Launch remains one application process per evidence run; resize calls are awaited serially by scenario steps.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Application reuse now includes extraEnv in its equality key, preventing reuse across different environments; identical options still reuse. Profile writes occur once before launch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Scenario usage frequency is test-only and bounded by authored steps.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: test-only boundaries are explicit, bounded, and do not multiply product work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 37 changed files and paginated large patches. Reported three diff-introduced issues: synchronous full-catalog working-set rebuilds on every sibling-chat switch, non-coalesced stale editor restores, and quadratic per-peer working-set serialization during session cleanup. Other storage, provider, startup, phone-transition, and test-automation paths were bounded or unchanged in expensive-boundary cardinality.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
